description: The most relevant number of the problem "wealth concentration" of the start page ranking and the potential solutions: the progressive surcharge on the wealth tax is capped at the rate that halves the largest wealth over 30 years, which follows from (1 - r)^30 = 0.5 and yields about 2.28 percent. The second solution is a proto basic income implemented as a negative income tax, whose labour supply effect was measured in the experiments of the 1970s.

words.name: concentration
words.description: the amount of a substance in a defined volume or mass

words.name: tax
words.description: compulsory financial charge to public authority

triples.name: wealth concentration
triples.description: concentration of money and power that destroys democratic participation (concept paper section 5)

triples.name: maximum wealth tax rate
triples.description: the cap of the progressive surcharge: the effective rate that would halve the largest wealth bracket over 30 years, so (1 - r)^30 = 0.5

triples.name: wealth surcharge
triples.description: a progressive surcharge on the wealth tax for the part of the net wealth that exceeds the value of a statistical life (concept paper section 5)

triples.name: basic income
triples.description: a proto unconditional basic income implemented as a negative income tax, started so low that almost nobody feels an effect and raised as long as the net effect stays positive (concept paper section 5)

sources.name: Robins (1985) negative income tax experiments
sources.description: Robins, P. K. (1985): A Comparison of the Labor Supply Findings from the Four Negative Income Tax Experiments. Cited by the concept paper section 5 together with Widerquist (2004) for an average labour supply reduction of about 5 percent.
